correctness.rationale: Every actual opinion flip strictly decreases an integer cut potential, proving absorption and validating triangular recurrences. Direct graph argument proves the n<=4 obstruction. Full labeled enumeration covers all 2^(n choose 2) masks for n=2..5, every nonedge and every binary coloring, with 2-to-5 connected counts 1,4,38,728 and n=5 exactly 90 creations of two edge-marked classes. Exact rational Markov recurrences compute 7/48 and 31/192 and times; an independent 32-state rational Gaussian linear-system solver reproduces them. Star recurrence derived by explicit competing update rates; the analytic hub-flip bound tends zero proving q_m to 1/4. Boundary conditions m>=4 and nonunanimous absorption are explicit.

originality.rationale: Three materially inspected primary papers differ in update convention, graph regime, or central parameter. Comparing statements and implications, none contains a result entailing the precise five-vertex edge-created absorbing-polarization classification, four exact absorption/time values, or the star-family limit. Meaning-based records and available own claims were searched for same parameters, aliases and stronger coverage. Residual risk is explicitly retained rather than claiming exhaustive novelty.
residual_risks: An uncatalogued exact small-graph Ising/local-cut result may imply the five-vertex classification in a different terminology; searches cannot prove absolute novelty.
Related studies may use another tie convention with a special equivalence on a restricted subclass, though the inspected primary dynamics differ.
The 5-vertex minimum uses complete enumeration, but only a single algorithm enumerates graph types; the independent Markov-system check tests the two representatives, not the enumeration itself.

value.rationale: New social contact need not mitigate discord; under tie-retaining local best response it can generate previously impossible polarized absorbing equilibria. A sharp minimal agent count and complete two-type first layer are interpretable structural boundaries, reinforced by exact basin probabilities and a large-star family where the new edge keeps a nonvanishing 1/4 effect. Unlike a routine isolated counterexample, the first-layer classification and asymptotic persistence address whether the effect survives network scaling. No empirical societal inference is made.
